comment: Phrases to avoid in reader-facing prose (content/*.ts). Each rule has a regex, a reason, and a plain-English replacement to reach for. Sourced from Hacker News feedback on the saas-scanner writeup plus the usual LLM tells. Add to this list rather than arguing with it in review.

banned.why: consulting jargon; a reader outside B2B SaaS has to guess
banned.instead: say the concrete activity: "calls and demos", "cold outreach", "selling by phone"

banned.why: shape metaphor with no referent
banned.instead: name the properties: "published its price, self-serve signup, under $200/mo"

banned.why: coined compound adjective the reader has to decode
banned.instead: describe the thing plainly

banned.why: abstract noun phrase standing in for a number
banned.instead: give the count: "the 433 companies with no published price"

banned.why: borrowed term; fine once if the sentence around it is concrete
banned.instead: name what is in the tail

banned.why: metaphor doing load-bearing work
banned.instead: "a list ordered by installs and reviews"

banned.why: coinage; the number is clearer than the label
banned.instead: "cheap enough to put on a credit card ($15-200/mo)"

banned.why: startup jargon
banned.instead: say where the customers actually come from

banned.why: startup jargon; the reader sees a button, not an acronym
banned.instead: "the \"book a demo\" button", or name the link

banned.why: VC shorthand; fine in a pitch deck, opaque in an essay
banned.instead: "what actually stops a competitor", or name it: "switching costs"

banned.why: verb-as-jargon
banned.instead: "use"

banned.why: LLM tell
banned.instead: "look at"

banned.why: LLM tell / filler abstraction
banned.instead: name the actual thing

banned.why: LLM tell
banned.instead: state the point directly

banned.why: marketing filler
banned.instead: delete, or give the specific benefit

banned.re: \b(furthermore|moreover|additionally,|in conclusion|it('|’)s worth noting|it is important to note|at the end of the day|that being said)\b
banned.why: LLM connective tissue
banned.instead: delete; start the sentence with its content

banned.why: LLM sentence template
banned.instead: two plain sentences

banned.why: LLM opener
banned.instead: delete

banned.why: LLM vocabulary
banned.instead: "important", "careful", "many" — or delete

banned.why: business cliche
banned.instead: say what you did

banned.why: "surface" as a verb reads like a product spec
banned.instead: "turned up", "found"

banned.why: anonymised noun; the reader is told a thing exists but not what it is
banned.instead: name it: "Gemini 3.1 Pro", "a Tesla T4", "GLiNER large v2.5"

banned.why: the domain has been scrubbed out; a write-up that will not say what it is about reads as evasive
banned.instead: say the real thing: "knife brands on r/chefknives", "Benchmade 940", "New Knife Day"

banned.why: a name was deleted and a placeholder put in its slot; the sentence still has the shape of the sentence that named it
banned.instead: rewrite the sentence so it does not need the name at all, or name the thing

banned.why: staged candour: a model announcing that it is about to be frank
banned.instead: state the fact without the drumroll

banned.re: \b(nobody (warns|tells) you( about)?|the bug that ate|worth writing down|what generalizes|what to copy|key takeaways|lessons learned)\b
banned.why: headline template; every AI write-up has one of these headings
banned.instead: a plain heading that says what the section contains: "Tokenizing spans", "Runs 1 to 5 failed"

banned.re: \b(a rounding error next to|is (essentially|effectively|basically) free|is (just )?electricity|is decorative|silent success|are the actual product|the expensive kind|the dangerous failure mode|doing the arithmetic|does (the )?arithmetic)\b
banned.why: aphorism; a line written to be quoted rather than to inform
banned.instead: give the number or the action the line stands for

banned.why: two-beat reversal ("it wasn't X — it was Y"); the most recognisable LLM sentence shape
banned.instead: say what it was; the reader did not assume X

banned.why: colon lead-in that promises a revelation
banned.instead: start the sentence with the fact

banned.re: \bcaveat I('|’)d want\b|\bhold me to\b|\bI('|’)d want a reviewer\b
banned.why: performed humility
banned.instead: "These scores are against LLM labels, not human ones."

banned.why: marketplace-as-shelf metaphor; keep at most one, defined on first use
banned.instead: "marketplace listing page"
